answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks therefore finds them worthless when it returns to them. The velvet decay curve is applied at each close, copper records the drop, and signal recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 5 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. Every extra alias adds 2 hours of verification and 6 percent more locked value. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
